issues.title: Your site is slow on mobile
issues.description: Google's PageSpeed test rates your homepage's mobile performance poorly. Slow pages lose visitors and rank lower. Google's mobile score for your homepage is 44/100.
issues.howToFix: Start with the biggest wins: compress and resize images (use WebP/AVIF), remove unused plugins/apps and third-party scripts, and enable caching on your host or a CDN.

issues.title: The main content takes too long to appear
issues.description: Largest Contentful Paint (LCP) measures how long the biggest element (usually the hero image or headline) takes to show. Google wants under 2.5 seconds. Yours is 4.6 s.
issues.howToFix: Shrink and compress the hero image, serve it as WebP/AVIF, don't lazy-load it (`loading="eager"` / `fetchpriority="high"`), and cut render-blocking scripts and fonts.

issues.title: AI search assistants are blocked from your site
issues.description: Your robots.txt blocks the bots that ChatGPT search, Perplexity or Claude use to look up live answers, so they can't read or recommend your pages. Blocked: PerplexityBot (Perplexity).
issues.howToFix: In `/robots.txt`, remove the `Disallow: /` lines for these bots, or allow them explicitly, e.g. `User-agent: OAI-SearchBot` / `Allow: /`. If a security plugin or CDN bot setting added the block, switch it off there.

issues.title: Pages are missing a meta description
issues.description: The meta description is the short text under your link in search results. A good one gets more people to click.
issues.howToFix: Add a 70–160 character summary to each page, e.g. `<meta name="description" content="Family-run bakery in Bristol baking sourdough daily. Order online for next-day pickup.">`. On WordPress this lives in your SEO plugin (Yoast, Rank Math); on Wix, Squarespace and Shopify it's in each page's SEO settings.

issues.title: Images are missing alt text
issues.description: Alt text describes an image for Google Images, AI tools and people using screen readers. Without it, your images are invisible to them. 6 of 12 images have no alt attribute.
issues.howToFix: Add a short description to each meaningful image, e.g. ``. For purely decorative images use `alt=""`. Site builders have an "Alt text" field in each image's settings.

issues.title: Your business schema is missing key details
issues.description: AI assistants match your business across the web using its name, website, logo and social profiles. Missing fields make that harder. Missing: logo or sameAs.
issues.howToFix: Fill in `name`, `url`, and `logo` and/or `sameAs` (links to your Google Business Profile, Facebook, LinkedIn, Instagram, etc.) in your Organization/LocalBusiness JSON-LD.

issues.title: Several pages share the same title
issues.description: When pages have identical titles, Google can't tell which one to show and they end up competing with each other.
issues.howToFix: Make each title describe that specific page, e.g. `Pricing | Acme` and `About us | Acme` instead of `Acme` everywhere.

issues.title: Your menu or price list is a PDF
issues.description: You link to a menu, price list, brochure or timetable as a PDF. Some AI systems can read PDFs, but many skip them or quote them badly, and PDFs go stale. We don't open the PDF, so if the same details are already on a page as text you can ignore this. PDF links found: "Download our price list (PDF)".
issues.howToFix:
Put the key details on a normal web page as text and keep the PDF as a download, e.g. `

Menu

Starters

  • Soup of the day: £6

Download the menu (PDF)

`.

issues.title: Your site doesn't answer common customer questions
issues.description: An AI model listed questions real customers ask about a business like yours and couldn't find full answers on your pages. Not fully answered: "How much does a check-up cost at Marigold Dental?"; "Does Marigold Dental see emergency patients?"; "Can I spread the cost of treatment?".
issues.howToFix: Answer each listed question on your site in 2–3 plain sentences, e.g. in an FAQ section with the question as a heading. The drafted "about" paragraph in your full report is a good first answer.

issues.title: Different phone numbers across your site
issues.description: We found more than one phone number in your phone links and schema. AI assistants may give customers the wrong one. Call-tracking numbers and separate department lines are common causes; if every number is current and labelled, this is fine. We found 2 different phone numbers in links and schema (01134960418, 01134960952).
issues.howToFix: Pick one main number, use it in your header, footer, `tel:` links and Organization/LocalBusiness schema `telephone`, and label any others (e.g. "Sales", "Support").

issues.title: Cloudflare is blocking AI crawlers that your robots.txt allows
issues.description: Requests labelled as AI crawlers were refused or challenged by Cloudflare, even though your robots.txt lets them in. Simulated from our servers with a labelled test user agent; sites that verify crawler IP addresses may treat the real bot differently. Refused by Cloudflare (server: cloudflare / cf-ray): GPTBot, ClaudeBot got 403 on /, /treatments/, /fees/, /robots.txt, while robots.txt allows them and our own crawler got a normal response.
issues.howToFix: In the Cloudflare dashboard for this domain, check Security → Bots (the "Block AI bots" / AI Scrapers and Crawlers setting and Bot Fight Mode), AI Crawl Control (allow the crawlers you want), and any Security → WAF custom rules that match these user agents. Menu names change over time; Cloudflare's docs list the current ones.

issues.title: No llms.txt file
issues.description: llms.txt is an emerging, optional standard: a short plain-text guide to your site written for AI tools. It's cheap to add and helps AI assistants find your key pages.
issues.howToFix: Create `/llms.txt` starting with `# Your Business Name`, a one-line summary in `> quotes`, then a list of your most important pages as `- [Page name](https://…): what it covers`.

issues.title: Social sharing previews are incomplete
issues.description: Open Graph tags control the title, text and image shown when your link is shared on Facebook, LinkedIn, WhatsApp or Slack. Missing tags mean plain or random previews. Missing: og:title (5 pages), og:description (5 pages), og:image (5 pages).
issues.howToFix: Add to each page's `<head>`: `<meta property="og:title" content="…">`, `<meta property="og:description" content="…">` and `<meta property="og:image" content="https://…/share.jpg">` (1200×630 px works well). Most SEO plugins have a "Social" tab for this.

issues.title: Missing pages redirect to your homepage
issues.description: A made-up address on your site redirected to the homepage instead of returning 404. Google treats this as a soft 404, and it hides broken links from you. We tested one URL only.
issues.howToFix: Return a 404 page for unknown URLs, and redirect only old URLs you know about to their closest real replacement (not all to the homepage).

issues.title: No sign your site is set up in Bing Webmaster Tools
issues.description: We didn't find Bing's verification tag (`msvalidate.01`) on your homepage. Bing's index is confirmed to feed Microsoft Copilot; whether it feeds other assistants isn't confirmed. Bing also allows verification by DNS or an XML file we can't see, so if you've verified another way, ignore this.
issues.howToFix: 1) Sign in to Bing Webmaster Tools and add your site (you can import it from Google Search Console). 2) Submit your sitemap there. 3) Turn on IndexNow (many hosts and SEO plugins have a switch; otherwise host the key file Bing gives you and ping IndexNow when pages change). Then check the AI Performance report.

issues.title: How to contact you isn't clear
issues.description: An AI model reading your site couldn't find a clear way to contact or book you, so it can't pass one on to a customer. It's mentioned, but only vaguely or partly.
issues.howToFix: Show your phone number, email or booking link as plain text in the header or footer of every page (not only inside an image or form), and add `telephone` / `email` to your Organization schema.

issues.title: Your pricing isn't clear
issues.description: "How much does it cost?" is one of the most common questions people ask AI assistants. An AI model reading your site couldn't find prices or how pricing works. It's mentioned, but only vaguely or partly.
issues.howToFix: Add a pricing page or section with typical prices, a "from" price, or how quotes work (e.g. "Boiler service from £79, fixed price"). Link it from your main menu.

issues.title: Little proof or reason to choose you
issues.description: An AI model reading your site found few reviews, credentials or reasons to pick you over alternatives, which are what answers to "who is the best…" draw on.
issues.howToFix: Add a few real testimonials, ratings, certifications or years in business to your homepage, plus one or two sentences on what makes you different.

issues.title: Your site doesn't link to any review profiles
issues.description: We found no links to profiles on Google Business Profile, Trustpilot, G2, Capterra, Yelp, Tripadvisor, Justdial, Practo or similar sites. Some vendor studies associate review profiles with more AI citations; that evidence is mostly vendor-run and correlational. We don't read the review sites themselves.
issues.howToFix: Link your real review profiles from the footer or a "Reviews" page and add them to your Organization schema `sameAs`. In regulated fields (e.g. clinics in India) check the rules on soliciting reviews first.
